To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the current computational techniques available to simulate biological systems have limitations, which are often not fully appreciated, and that there is a need to develop new computational methods to overcome these limitations.

(1) the spatial structure and the dynamics of proteins, nucleic acids and their assemblies are accurately predicted by molecular simulation; and (2) the spatial and temporal structure of the solvent is also predicted accurately.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the development of a comprehensive computational approach for the study of biomolecular systems at the atomistic scale.
developing a molecular-level description of the structure and function of biological systems, and the application of these models to the study of biological processes.
the development and application of computational methods to the study of biomolecular systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
there is no single technique that can provide a complete description of a system.
the current computational techniques available are not yet sufficiently accurate to be used as the only source of information for a detailed understanding of biomolecular systems.

, although there are many limitations, the current state of the art in computer simulation is sufficiently mature that it can be considered a useful and important complement to the other biophysical methods that are currently available.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a computational approach for the study of biomolecules that is capable of describing the spatial and temporal behavior of biomolecules in solution at the level of individual atoms.

the computational tools we have developed and used in our laboratory have been very successful in providing detailed atomistic models of biomolecules that are in good quantitative agreement with experiment.
the current level of accuracy in the simulation of biomolecules is not sufficient to provide a detailed understanding of biological function.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the most accurate simulations are those that are most closely matched to the experimental conditions of the biological system.
we can use the power of computer simulation to understand the molecular details that underlie biological processes and that this can be done in a way that is complementary to experiment.
the most successful simulations of biomolecules are those that are most closely matched to the experiment.
